name: api_getAllBackup
description:
**Pick this tool for backup INVENTORY and backup HISTORY questions.**

This tool lists backups available in the configured Catalyst Center backup storage with optional filtering, sorting, and pagination. It returns backup identifiers plus summary fields such as status, dates, size, scope, storage, compatibility, and availability.

**Use this tool when the user asks:**
- to show all backups or available backups
- whether there are failed backups
- which backups are available for restore
- for backup history or recent backups
- for backups created by a specific user, status, or time period
- for a list of backups before drilling into one backup in detail

**Pick this tool for questions like:**
- "Show me all backups"
- "List available backups"
- "Are there any failed backups?"
- "What backups can be restored?"
- "Show the latest backups"
- "Show backups created by system"
- "List backups from the last week"

**Do NOT use this tool for:**
- current backup configuration/settings
- mounted backup storage capacity questions
- configured NFS server health
- detailed diagnostics for one backup execution

When the user wants full package, version, or compatibility details for a single backup, first call this tool to get the backup `id`, then call `api_getBackupById`.

name: api_getBackupById
description:
**Pick this tool for ONE specific backup when you already know the backup ID.**

This tool retrieves the full details for a specific backup by backup UUID, including installed packages, versions, compatibility errors, storage details, size, dates, and restore compatibility.

**Use this tool when the user asks:**
- for full details of one known backup
- what packages or versions are included in a backup
- whether a specific backup is compatible for restore
- when a specific backup was created and by whom
- for the storage or scope details of a specific backup

**Pick this tool for questions like:**
- "Show details for backup <id>"
- "What packages are in backup <id>?"
- "Is backup <id> compatible for restore?"
- "When was backup <id> created?"
- "Show me everything about backup <id>"

**Do NOT use this tool for:**
- discovering which backups exist
- listing all backups or failed backups
- backup execution history

This is the detail view for a known backup. If the identifier is unknown, call `api_getAllBackup` first to obtain the backup `id`.

name: api_getBackupConfiguration
description:
**Pick this tool for backup SETTINGS and configuration questions.**

This tool retrieves the current Catalyst Center backup configuration, including retention policy, configured storage type, mount path, and whether an encryption passphrase is available.

**Use this tool when the user asks:**
- whether backups are configured
- what the backup retention policy is
- what storage backend or mount path is configured for backups
- whether an encryption passphrase is available for backups
- what the current backup settings are

**Pick this tool for questions like:**
- "Is backup configured on this cluster?"
- "What is the backup retention policy?"
- "What backup settings are configured?"
- "What mount path is configured for backups?"
- "Is an encryption passphrase configured for backup?"

**Do NOT use this tool for:**
- listing historical backups or available backups
- backup or restore job history
- NFS server health or unhealthy nodes

Use `api_getAllBackup` for backup inventory/history and `api_getNfsConfigurations` for NFS backup server health details.

name: api_getBackupRestoreExecution
description:
**Pick this tool for ONE specific backup or restore execution when you already know the execution ID.**

This tool retrieves the full details for one backup or restore execution by execution UUID, including error diagnostics, task-level details, status, timing, and failure information.

**Use this tool when the user asks:**
- why a specific backup execution failed
- why a specific restore execution failed
- for detailed status of one execution
- for task-by-task details of one execution
- for error codes or error messages for one known execution

**Pick this tool for questions like:**
- "Why did backup execution <id> fail?"
- "Show details for restore job <id>"
- "What tasks ran in execution <id>?"
- "Give me the error for backup execution <id>"
- "Show execution diagnostics for <id>"

**Do NOT use this tool for:**
- listing all backup jobs or restore jobs
- discovering execution IDs
- listing available backups

Obtain the execution identifier from `api_getBackupRestoreExecutions`.

name: api_getBackupRestoreExecutions
description:
**Pick this tool for backup JOB HISTORY and restore JOB HISTORY questions.**

This tool lists backup and restore execution history with optional filtering by backup, job type, status, pagination, and sorting.

**Use this tool when the user asks:**
- about backup jobs or restore jobs
- for failed backup executions or failed restore attempts
- whether any backup or restore job is in progress
- for execution history for a known backup
- for restore attempts, delete-backup jobs, or job status trends

**Pick this tool for questions like:**
- "Show me backup jobs"
- "List restore attempts"
- "Are there any backups in progress?"
- "Which backup jobs failed?"
- "Show execution history for backup <id>"
- "List failed restore jobs"
- "Show recent backup executions"

**Do NOT use this tool for:**
- listing available backups themselves
- backup configuration/settings
- mounted backup storage capacity
- detailed diagnostics for one specific execution after you already have the execution ID

This is the list view for executions. When the user needs detailed diagnostics for one execution, first obtain the execution `id` here and then call `api_getBackupRestoreExecution`.

name: api_getBackupStorages

**Pick this tool for mounted BACKUP STORAGE CAPACITY and backup disk usage questions.**

This tool retrieves mounted backup storage information such as mount point, filesystem details, total capacity, used capacity, and usage percentage for a specific storage type.

**Use this tool when the user asks:**
- how much backup space is available
- how full the backup disk or backup storage is
- what mount point is used for backup storage
- what mounted storage backend is used for backups
- for NFS, physical disk, or remote server backup storage capacity details

**Pick this tool for questions like:**
- "How much backup space is available?"
- "Show backup storage usage"
- "How full is the backup disk?"
- "What backup storage is mounted?"
- "Show NFS backup storage capacity"
- "What is the free space on backup storage?"

**Do NOT use this tool for:**
- backup configuration settings like retention policy
- listing available backups
- backup or restore execution history
- configured NFS server definitions or unhealthy nodes

If the user asks generally about backup storage and does not specify a type, default to `NFS`. Use `api_getNfsConfigurations` instead when the question is about configured NFS servers and their health rather than mounted storage capacity.

name: api_getEoXDetailsPerDevice
description:
**MANDATORY PREREQUISITE:** For site-scoped EOX queries, you MUST call `api_getSites` before `get_device_details`, and you MUST call `get_device_details` before `api_getEoXDetailsPerDevice`.

**Steps:**
1. Call `api_getSites` with the user-specified site name.
2. Extract the `nameHierarchy` from the `api_getSites` response.
3. Call `get_device_details` with `siteHierarchy` set to the extracted `nameHierarchy` to retrieve the devices in that site.
4. Extract the `deviceId` or device UUID for each matching device from the `get_device_details` response.
5. Call `api_getEoXDetailsPerDevice` with `deviceId` set to each resolved device UUID.
6. Use the returned per-device EOX details or per-device `alertCount` values to answer the user's site-scoped EOX question.

**Exception:** Skip step 1 if the user already provides an exact site hierarchy value that can be passed directly as `siteHierarchy` to `get_device_details`. Skip steps 1-3 if the user already provides a valid device UUID directly for a specific device.

**Returns:** Detailed EOX information for a specific device, including per-device alert count, alert details, alert type, bulletin information, lifecycle dates, scan status, comments, and last scan time. For site-scoped questions, this tool should be executed after resolving the site to devices and then called once per device.

name: api_getEoXStatusForAllDevices
description:
Use this API for network-wide, device-level retrieval of EOX information when the user wants to display, list, fetch, report, review, or enumerate EOX alerts or EOX status across all devices, every device, or all network devices. It is the correct API for complete per-device EOX alert coverage across the network, including which devices have alerts, each device's alert count, per-device hardware/software/module EOX type breakdown, scan status, comments, and last scan time. This API returns a collection of device records for device-by-device EOX alert visibility across the network, not aggregate network totals.

**MANDATORY POST-PROCESSING:** The returned `deviceId` is for internal lookup only and must not be shown in user-facing output. For every device record that will be included in the response, call `get_device_details` with `device_id` set to the returned `deviceId`, resolve the device name and management IPv4 address, and present the device name or management IP instead of the raw internal identifier.

**Steps:**
1. Call `api_getEoXStatusForAllDevices`
2. Read the returned per-device EOX records
3. For each returned `deviceId`, call `get_device_details` with `device_id` equal to that value
4. Use the resolved device name and/or management IPv4 address in the final response
5. Do not expose raw `deviceId` values unless the user explicitly asks for internal UUIDs

**Exception:** If the user explicitly asks for internal device identifiers, the raw `deviceId` may be included. Do not use this API when the user only needs summary counts such as overall hardware, software, module, or total EOX alert counts.

name: api_getTag
description:
**TAG DEFINITION LISTING RULE:**
- Use this API to enumerate existing tag definitions when the user asks for available, existing, default/system, or custom/user-created tags.
- For an unfiltered tag-definition inventory, omit both `name` and `systemTag`.
- Use `systemTag=true` only for system-created/default tag definitions, and `systemTag=false` only for user-created/custom tag definitions.
- Do not use `api_getTagResourceTypes` for tag-definition inventory; that tool returns taggable object categories, not existing tag records.
**TAG PHRASE INTERPRETATION RULE:**
- When the user says `tag <value>`, `tagged <value>`, `tagged with <value>`, `tagged as <value>`, `with <value> tag`, `under tag <value>`, or `in tag <value>`, treat `<value>` as a tag name and pass that literal value to `name`.
- Tag names can look like switch names, device labels, site names, interface labels, operational states, or camelCase words. The presence of words like switch, device, site, port, interface, up, or down inside the value does not change it into a device/site/interface lookup when the user introduced it as a tag.
- Do not reinterpret a tag name as a switch, hostname, site, interface, IP address, or inventory search term.

**NAMED-TAG RESOLVER RULE:**
- Use this API first when the user gives a human-readable tag name and asks for devices, ports, interfaces, or member counts inside that tag.
- This tool resolves the tag name to a tag UUID. It is not the final answer tool for member questions.
- After a successful response containing an `id`, immediately call exactly one companion member tool:
  - `api_getTagMembersById` for list/show/get/find/which/what member requests.
  - `api_getTagMemberCount` for count/how-many/total/number member requests.
- For device membership, the companion tool must use `memberType="networkdevice"`.
- For port or interface membership, the companion tool must use `memberType="interface"`.
- Repeating `api_getTag` with the same tag name after a UUID has been returned is incorrect; move to the companion member tool.

**DO NOT SUBSTITUTE:**
- Do not use `api_getTagCount` for named-tag member counts; it counts tag definitions, not members.
- Do not use `api_getInterfaces` or generic device/interface inventory tools to answer which resources are in one tag.
- Do not use inverse association tools when the user wants tag-to-member lookup.
- Do not start with `api_getTagResourceTypes`, site tools, or knowledge-base fallback for live named-tag membership questions.
- Do not reuse the tag name as a site name, device name, interface name, IP address, or UUID.

**TAG + SITE OR COMPLIANCE NOTE:**
- If a request combines a named tag with a site or compliance filter, this API still only resolves the tag UUID. Ground the tag by calling `api_getTagMembersById` with that UUID before applying site or compliance filtering.

name: api_getTagById
description: Returns tag specified by Id

name: api_getTagCount
description:
**TAG PHRASE EXCLUSION:**
- If the user asks how many/count/total/number of devices, network devices, ports, or interfaces are `tagged`, `with <value> tag`, `under tag <value>`, or `in tag <value>`, do not use this tool. The value is a tag name for a member-count workflow, not a tag-definition count filter.
- Use `api_getTag` followed by `api_getTagMemberCount` for named-tag member counts, even when the tag name looks like a switch, device, site, port, interface, or operational state.

"How many tag definitions exist?" "Count user-created tags" "How many system tags are there?" — USE THIS API only for counting TAG DEFINITIONS.

This API returns the count of tag definitions. It does NOT return the number of devices, ports, or interfaces inside a tag.

**MANDATORY — USE THIS API FOR:**
- total tag count
- count of user-created or system-created tags
- how many tag definitions match a given name
- questions about whether duplicate tag definitions exist

**DO NOT USE THIS API FOR:**
- "How many devices are tagged with <tag name>?"
- "What's the count of devices with <tag name> tag?"
- "How many ports are tagged with <tag name>?"
- "How many interfaces are tagged with <tag name>?"
- "How many ports/interfaces are tagged with <tag name>?"
- "List devices in tag <tag name>"
- "Show interfaces in tag <tag name>"
- Any named-tag membership question

**NEGATIVE FEW-SHOT EXAMPLES:**
- User: "What's the count of devices with <tag name> tag?" -> do NOT use `api_getTagCount`; use `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMemberCount`
- User: "How many ports are tagged with <tag name>?" -> do NOT use `api_getTagCount`; use `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMemberCount`

For named-tag member counts, the correct route is:
1. `api_getTag(name=<tag_name>)`
2. extract the UUID
3. `api_getTagMemberCount(id=<UUID>, memberType=<networkdevice_or_interface>)`

**WRONG ROUTING TO AVOID:**
- Never use `api_getTagCount` just because the question contains "count", "how many", or "total".
- Never use `api_getTagCount` for device-count or interface-count questions inside a tag.
- STOP and switch to `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMemberCount` when the question is about members of a named tag.

name: api_getTagMemberCount
description:
**TAG MEMBER COUNT TOOL:**
- Select this tool together with `api_getTag` when the user provides a human-readable tag name and asks how many, count, total, or number of members are inside that tag.
- Execute this tool after `api_getTag` returns the tag UUID. This tool requires a UUID in `id`; never pass the tag name as `id`.
- Use this for counts of devices, ports, or interfaces inside one named tag.
- Use `memberType="networkdevice"` when counting devices.
- Use `memberType="interface"` when counting ports or interfaces.
**TAG NAME DISAMBIGUATION:**
- If the request uses `tag`, `tagged`, `with <value> tag`, `under tag`, or `in tag` and asks how many/count/total/number of devices, network devices, ports, or interfaces belong to that value, select this tool with `api_getTag`.
- The value introduced by the tag phrase remains a tag name even if it contains words like switch, device, site, port, interface, up, or down. Do not route it to site, device, interface, inventory count, or tag-definition count tools.
- For device counts inside the tag, use `memberType="networkdevice"`. For port or interface counts inside the tag, use `memberType="interface"`.

**REQUIRED WORKFLOW:**
1. `api_getTag(name=<tag_name>)`
2. Extract the returned tag UUID.
3. `api_getTagMemberCount(id=<UUID>, memberType=<networkdevice_or_interface>)`

**DO NOT SUBSTITUTE:**
- Do not use `api_getTagCount`; that counts tag definitions, not members inside one tag.
- Do not use generic device counts, onboarding counts, compliance counts, or field-notice counts for named-tag member counts.
- Do not use inverse tag-association tools or generic inventory tools to reconstruct a count indirectly.
- Do not leave the workflow at `api_getTag`, and do not keep calling `api_getTag` repeatedly after the UUID has already been resolved.
- Do not use this tool for list/show/which member questions; use `api_getTagMembersById` after `api_getTag` instead.
- Do not fall back to generic KB guidance for live named-tag count questions.

name: api_getTagMembersById
description:
**TAG MEMBER LISTING TOOL:**
- Select this tool together with `api_getTag` when the user provides a human-readable tag name and asks to list, show, get, find, identify, or ask what/which members are inside that tag.
- Execute this tool after `api_getTag` returns the tag UUID. This tool requires a UUID in `id`; never pass the tag name as `id`.
- Use this for tag-to-device and tag-to-interface/tag-to-port listing workflows.
- Use `memberType="networkdevice"` when the requested members are devices.
- Use `memberType="interface"` when the requested members are ports or interfaces.
**TAG NAME DISAMBIGUATION:**
- If the request uses `tag`, `tagged`, `with <value> tag`, `under tag`, or `in tag` and asks which/list/show/get devices, network devices, ports, or interfaces belong to that value, select this tool with `api_getTag`.
- The value introduced by the tag phrase remains a tag name even if it contains words like switch, device, site, port, interface, up, or down. Do not route it to site, device, interface, or inventory lookup tools.
- For devices or network devices inside the tag, use `memberType="networkdevice"`. For ports or interfaces inside the tag, use `memberType="interface"`.

**REQUIRED WORKFLOW:**
1. `api_getTag(name=<tag_name>)`
2. Extract the returned tag UUID.
3. `api_getTagMembersById(id=<UUID>, memberType=<networkdevice_or_interface>)`

**DO NOT SUBSTITUTE:**
- Do not use this tool for count/how-many/total/number questions; use `api_getTagMemberCount` after `api_getTag` instead.
- Do not leave the workflow at `api_getTag`; once the UUID is known, this tool performs the member lookup.
- Do not keep calling `api_getTag` repeatedly after the UUID has already been resolved.
- Do not use `api_getInterfaces`, generic device inventory, site lookup, resource-type discovery, or inverse tag-association tools when the user wants members of one named tag.
- Do not fall back to generic KB guidance for live named-tag membership.

**TAG + SITE OR COMPLIANCE NOTE:**
- This API returns tag-scoped members. If the user also names a site or asks for compliance, intersect these tag members with the requested site or compliance filter before forming the final answer.

name: api_getTagResourceTypes
description:
**TAG PHRASE EXCLUSION:**
- If the user names one tag with `tag`, `tagged`, `with <value> tag`, `under tag`, or `in tag` and asks for devices, ports, interfaces, or counts, do not use this tool. The request is about members of one tag, not taggable resource categories.
- Use `api_getTag` followed by `api_getTagMembersById` or `api_getTagMemberCount` for named-tag membership workflows.

Returns the supported resource categories that can be tagged in Cisco Catalyst Center, such as what kinds of entities are taggable. Use this tool only when the user asks about supported taggable resource types or categories.

**NOT FOR TAG INVENTORY:**
- Do not use this tool when the user asks to enumerate existing tag definitions or tag records.
- Do not use this tool for system/default tags or user-created/custom tags.
- Use `api_getTag` for tag-definition inventory; this tool is only for taggable resource-category capability questions.

This tool does NOT resolve a tag name, does NOT return a tag UUID, and does NOT return the members inside one named tag.

**USE THIS TOOL ONLY FOR:**
- "What resource types can be tagged?"
- "Which kinds of objects support tags?"
- category-level capability questions about taggable entities

**DO NOT USE THIS TOOL FOR:**
- "Which devices have tag <tag name>?"
- "List devices tagged as <tag name>"
- "Get devices under tag <tag name>"
- "How many devices are tagged with <tag name>?"
- any request about the members inside one specific named tag

If the request names one tag and asks for devices, interfaces, ports, or counts, the correct route is:
1. `api_getTag(name=<tag_name>)`
2. then `api_getTagMembersById` or `api_getTagMemberCount`

**STOP CONDITIONS:**
- STOP if the user provided a specific tag name and wants members or counts.
- STOP if you are about to loop on resource-type discovery instead of resolving the tag with `api_getTag`.

**Licensing Smart Account Details**. Retrieve Licensing Smart Account information (name, id, domain, status).

**Execution Policy (MANDATORY):**

- Do NOT ask users whether they mean Licensing or PnP Smart Accounts.
- Treat Smart Account queries in this agent as Licensing context.

**Use Cases:**
- Listing available Licensing Smart Accounts
- Resolving Smart Account Name -> Smart Account ID
- Checking Smart Account status/details
- Preparing IDs for dependent licensing tools such as `api_readNetworkDeviceLicenses`, `api_virtualAccountDetails`, and `api_getLicenseUsage`.

**Dependency Guidance:**

name: api_systemLicensingLastOperationStatus
description:
**Tool Dependency: NONE**

Retrieves the task completion status of the last/most recent licensing operation or task executed for Cisco Catalyst Center system. This is a standalone API with no prerequisites.

**Use Cases:**
Use when checking, verifying, or getting the status of completed or in-progress smart licensing operations, tasks, or jobs such as:
- System registration operations/tasks (whether system registration completed, succeeded, failed)
- System authorization operations/tasks (whether authorization renewal completed)
- Any smart licensing related task execution status

**What This API Does:**
Returns task execution details:
- status: PENDING (task in progress), SUCCESS (task completed successfully), FAILURE (task failed)
- isError: true (failed), false (succeeded)
- failureReason: explanation of why task failed
- errorCode: error identifier if applicable
- taskId: unique task identifier
- lastUpdate: timestamp of last status update

**IMPORTANT DISTINCTION:**
This API provides TASK/OPERATION completion status (whether an operation finished), NOT the current authorization/compliance status of the system. For current system authorization/compliance/registration state (AUTHORIZED, OUT_OF_COMPLIANCE, REGISTERED, etc.), use `api_systemLicensingStatus` instead.

**When to Use:**
- After initiating a licensing operation to check if it completed
- Troubleshooting failed licensing tasks
- Monitoring in-progress licensing operations
- Getting the most recent task execution results

**Do NOT:**
- Use this API to check current system authorization status (use `api_systemLicensingStatus`)
- Use this API to check current compliance status (use `api_systemLicensingStatus`)
- Use this API to get registration status (use `api_systemLicensingStatus`)
- Confuse task completion status with system operational status

name: api_virtualAccountDetails
description:
**Licensing Virtual Account Details** (Tool Dependency: CRITICAL). Retrieve Virtual Account details for a specific Licensing Smart Account.

**Execution Policy (MANDATORY):**
- Use this tool directly for licensing virtual-account queries.
- Do NOT ask users whether they mean Licensing or PnP Smart Accounts.
- Treat this tool as Licensing context only.

**REQUIRED PRE-REQUISITE:**
You MUST call `api_smartAccountDetails` BEFORE calling `api_virtualAccountDetails`.

**Step-by-step process:**
1. Invoke `api_smartAccountDetails` to retrieve smart accounts.
2. Extract the `id` from the matched smart account.
3. Invoke `api_virtualAccountDetails` with `smart_account_id` set to the resolved ID.
4. If searching for a specific virtual account name and not found, repeat for other Smart Account IDs as needed.

**Do NOT:**
- Use this tool to list Smart Accounts (use `api_smartAccountDetails`)
- Call this tool without a valid Smart Account ID
